Components / Surfaces

Finder

.dr-finder · __services · __card · __actions · .dr-grouptab--icon · .dr-route · --single · __row · __mark · __open · __label · __value · __swap · .dr-when · __cell · __text · __label · __value · components/card.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Find
  1. 1.dr-finder__servicesThe service badges: an in-page tab worn by a radio, 32 visible inside a 44 target. Chosen is --on-action on --color-action at 9.46:1; idle is --slate on --media at 5.51:1. The row scrolls sideways rather than wrapping.
  2. 2.dr-finder__cardOne --card for where and when, so the questions read as one answer being assembled. A hairline separates the address rows from Date · Time. Measured 341.4 × 176.4 for delivery.
  3. 3.dr-route__openA route row is a <button aria-haspopup="dialog"> that opens the address picker. The label is 12/400 at 5.95:1. The value is 15/600 --ink at 14.37:1 once an address is taken, and the placeholder is --text-muted at 400 while the row is empty (data-empty). Rows are 341 × 58.8.
  4. 4.dr-route__swapA 44 × 44 icon button on the seam between From and To, named Swap pickup and drop-off.
  5. 5.dr-whenDate · Time: two buttons split by one rule, each opening its own drawer. Each half is 170.7 × 58.8. The button's name is its drawn text, Date Today (WCAG 2.5.3).
  6. 6.dr-finder__actionsFilters over Find, each 341 × 44, 8 apart. Find is the primary control, 4.93% of the frame.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Search home.

States

No state of its own: the finder is a container, and its controls are other components. The service badges take the in-page tabs states, and Filters, Find and the swap disc the button states. The route rows and the Date · Time cells carry only the keyboard ring: no hover, pressed or disabled look is declared for them.

When to use

The finder is the home screen, listings. It replaced the list of cards with one form that asks three questions: what, from where to where, and when. Each row is a button that opens a drawer: the address picker, the date picker, or the time drawer. Filters opens the filters drawer, and applied filters stand as chips above it. Find opens results on the map for the chosen service. The finder stands on four files: listings, listings-filters (the filters drawer open over it), listings-error and listings-loading. All four build the same three badges, with Delivery chosen at rest. On -error and -loading the route is filled in (Podil, 21 to Osokorky, 14). On -loading, Find becomes a disabled Searching… button and a status line names the place.

Home's solid green measures 6.08%: Find 4.93%, the chosen badge 1.05%, and the bell's count 0.11%. The solid green service badge beside Find is the designer's deliberate choice. It takes home over the ~5% guide, and that is how she wants it. The badge's mark is 1.41:1 against the idle fill, short of the 3:1 in WCAG 1.4.11. The label changing colour carries the state. The count badge on Filters (.dr-finder__actions … .dr-count-badge) is still declared and applies to nothing. The count moved off the button into the applied-filter chips (.dr-fchips), which stand between the card and Filters, hidden while nothing is applied.

Labels name the question in one word: From, To, Where, Date, Time. Placeholders name what goes there: Pickup address, Drop-off address, Address. Defaults are facts: Today, Now. The services are Delivery, Photo & video and Inspection. The two actions are Filters and Find.

Sources: DESIGN.md § The search home · inventory.md § 1 Search home · microcopy.md § listings, Search · ui/kit.html § The finder

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Each row is a button that shows its label and its value, and it opens the address drawer when tapped, never when it gets focus (WCAG 3.2.1). The whole row is the target. The swap keeps its own 44 above the row.

Don’t

Find

Filters and Find split across one row. They stood that way at 166.5 × 44 until the designer stacked them. A split row is where labels wrap. Keep them in .dr-finder__actions, each the full width. To choose between routes that leave the screen, use a choice card, not the finder.
